newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-WINGED FOOT TOUGH BUT FAIR, SAYS NOBILO.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WINGED FOOT TOUGH BUT FAIR, SAYS NOBILO.

text.p: MAMARONECK, New York, Aug 12 - Frank Nobilo believes Winged Foot golf course, venue of the United States PGA Championship, will embarrass a lot of the world's best players this weekend, NZPA reports.
Nobilo, New Zealand's only player in the final major championship of the year, has played two practice rounds on the 6389m championship course and knows he's in for a tough week.
"This course is going to embarrass a lot of players and Winged Foot, I think, is even tougher than Congressional," said Nobilo, referring to the venue for last June's US Open.
"It's still a fantastic golf course but probably the fairest toughest course I've ever seen."
Fuzzy Zoeller holds the official course record of four-under-par 66, shot during the 1984 US Open, a tournament made famous for Greg Norman waving a white towel in mock surrender during one round.
Mark Brooks, the defending US PGA champion, described Winged Foot as a mixture of six hard holes, six very hard holes and six impossible holes. Nobilo agrees.
"The course is so tough, you have to hit a lot of drivers and three woods, just about on every hole, and every time you hit in the rough, you are going to take a bogey," Nobilo said.
"So the thing is not only to get the ball in play, but you have to drive it straight and that does not mean short.

"You are going to have to play great golf because every shot is demanding, except probably for one hole and that's the short par-four sixth (296m) where you'll probably be hitting three iron and then a sand iron into the green.
"But every other hole, you have to hit your best drive because not only do you have to hit the ball long, you have to put it in the right position, and from there the greens are quite small targets."
Nobilo said Winged Foot reminded him of Shinnecock Hills, venue of the 1995 US Open where he finished 10th.
"There were holes out on the back nine of Shinnecock that if you were off line, you were history and this is the case here," he said.

"You finish one great par-four here, and then you walk to the next and stand on the tee and that hole is equally as good, and no hole is straight either, they each either bend a little to the right or a little to the left, so therefore the course doesn't favour any one player."

What does favour Nobilo is two excellent opening-round tee times. He will be grouped with Sweden's Jesper Parnevik and American Fred Couples for the first two rounds, and tees off at 8.10am local time (12.10am NZT) on Thursday and at 12.22pm (4.22am NZT).
"I've got a very good draw with Freddie (Couples) and Jesper (Parnevik) and I've got good tee times, so I've got my fingers crossed. I'm already raring to go."
